recovery_analysis.thesis: 9M26 revenue grew +11.5% YoY to SAR 87.2bn (Q3 SAR 35.0bn, +12.9% YoY) and 9M net profit rose +4.3% YoY to SAR 12.1bn (Q3 SAR 5.35bn) driven by an expanding regulated asset base (RAB) and lower ECL provisions. Strategic Saudi grid monopoly with A1/A sovereign-linked credit quality. Structural recovery anchored by Saudi Arabia utilities asset perimeter and SECO 4.723% 2028 seniority.

annotations.note: 9M26 rev SAR 87.2bn, EBITDA SAR 34.7bn, NPAT SAR 12.1bn, RAB SAR 278.8bn (+16.6% YoY), adj capex SAR 59.6bn.
Revenues secured by long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) or regulated tariff frameworks, providing hard-currency indexation and guaranteed minimum volume off-take.
Heavy generation transition capex peaks in 2024-2025; multi-year FCF inflects strongly positive as commercial operations commence.
Strategic national utility champions benefit from government balancing accounts or explicit fuel supply guarantees, mitigating commodity price volatility.

verdict.stance: Neutral / Sovereign-Anchored Grid Monopoly (A1/A) Amid Heavy Capex
verdict.summary: 9M26 revenue grew +11.5% YoY to SAR 87.2bn (Q3 SAR 35.0bn, +12.9% YoY) and 9M net profit rose +4.3% YoY to SAR 12.1bn (Q3 SAR 5.35bn) driven by an expanding regulated asset base (RAB) and lower ECL provisions. Strategic Saudi grid monopoly with A1/A sovereign-linked credit quality.

positives: Near-sovereign Saudi credit quality (A1/A, ~81% PIF/Government owned) and regulated asset base (RAB) formula.
Consistent top-line and profit growth: 9M26 rev +11.5% to SAR 87.2bn, NI +4.3% to SAR 12.1bn.
negatives: Massive multi-year grid & Vision 2030 renewables integration capex sustains negative pre-financing FCF.
Reliance on regular Mudaraba/government support instruments and sukuk market issuance.
Tight spread compression leaves limited upside vs KSA sovereign.
